As part of evaluating robustness against adversarial and poisoning attacks, the authors compare a GAN-based attack alongside label-flipping and random-swapping poisoning attacks. CTGAN is run as the generator to model tabular data and produce 5000 synthetic adversarial samples for the GAN-based attack scenario, used as one of several attack methods tested against the system.

paper-what-analysis-framework-digital-20.summary: This paper proposes a three-layer digital twin network architecture for 6G wireless management that implements a 'what-if analysis' module aligned with the FCAPS model, using NS-3 for the physical twin and ML/RL for the service layer. The framework generates synthetic scenario data (new users, connections, traffic patterns) to test throughput, latency, packet loss, and coverage under hypothetical network conditions, reporting a 43% improvement in a composite performance score from the CTGAN-based scenarios. CTGAN, described with its mode-specific normalization and conditional generator for categorical features, is run directly as the synthetic data generator underpinning the entire what-if analysis framework.

TGAN is cited among the existing deep generative models used as a comparison baseline for tabular synthetic data generation.

paper-reconstruction-attack-against-prin.summary: This paper studies privacy attacks against Principal Component Analysis, showing that an adversary who intercepts some principal components can mount a full data reconstruction attack, more severe than a prior membership inference attack against PCA. As a candidate protection mechanism, the authors propose that the data guardian first generate synthetic data and compute the principal components on it instead of the raw data, and they compare this defense against Differentially Private PCA. CTGAN is used throughout the empirical work both to synthesize the shadow dataset the attacker exploits and to generate the protective synthetic data whose mode-specific normalization and conditional vector mechanisms are described, making it the generator underlying all reported reconstruction-accuracy results.

paper-encode-ensemble-contextual-bandits.summary: This paper proposes ENCODE, an ensemble-based contextual bandit model combining LinUCB, Vowpal Wabbit, Contextual Thompson Sampling, and BayesUCB for dynamic pricing of kids' clothing in large-scale e-commerce, achieving margin improvements over standalone bandit algorithms. The primary dataset is described as synthetically generated based on models derived from a large kids' clothing e-commerce retailer, with the SDV paper cited only as the reference for the synthetic data generation approach. The citation to the original Synthetic Data Vault paper appears solely in the bibliography and is not otherwise engaged with in the text.

paper-housing-gans-market-data-2023.summary: Applies tabular adversarial generation to US housing market records so that price and regional data can be shared without privacy concerns, sampled on demand under user-specified conditions, and used to explore hypothetical market scenarios that the observed record does not cover. The model the paper calls Housing GANs is CTGAN applied to this domain: the methodology reproduces Xu et al.'s mode-specific normalization, the cond vector definition and the log-frequency training-by-sampling scheme as the machinery it uses, with no architectural change proposed.

paper-privacy-preserving-sharing-agricul.summary: This paper proposes a framework for enforcing agricultural data-privacy policy rules within privacy-preserving synthetic data generation, extracting constraints from EU codes of conduct and GDPR to bound a generative model, then evaluating the resulting synthetic agricultural data for downstream utility and resistance to re-identification/linkage attacks. TGAN (tabular GAN for synthesizing tabular data with GANs) appears only in the reference list alongside CTGAN, with no SDV-family term found anywhere in the body text. The citation to TGAN is bibliographic only, not tied to any run experiment.

paper-protecting-multiple-sensitive-attr.summary: This paper extends a Bayesian-network-based synthetic data generation approach (built on DataSynthesizer) to protect multiple sensitive attributes from inference attacks while preserving data utility, evaluating two extension techniques on micro-data. The proposed methods are entirely based on Bayesian Networks, not on SDV; the Synthetic Data Vault (Gaussian copula based) is only cited as one of several existing synthetic data generation approaches and noted as a possible future direction for extending the sensitive-attribute protection technique, without being run.

paper-tabular-augmentation-video-detecti.summary: This work addresses automated detection of hypomimia (reduced facial expressivity) in Parkinson's disease from video-derived tabular features, proposing a data augmentation pipeline to address limited sample sizes in this clinical dataset. The paper cites the CTGAN paper in connection with generating synthetic tabular samples to augment the training data used for classification. CTGAN is used as the generator producing synthetic tabular feature vectors for the augmentation experiments.

paper-autonomous-cybersecurity-intellige.summary: This paper proposes an AutoML-based Intrusion Detection System (IDS) framework that automates data pre-processing, feature engineering, model selection, hyperparameter tuning, and model ensembling for network security, evaluated on CICIDS2017 and 5G-NIDD datasets. The authors state their framework was built in Python by extending several ML libraries including the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), and its Automated Data Pre-processing component uses the Tabular Variational Auto-Encoder (TVAE) to synthesize minority-class samples for data balancing. SDV's TVAE synthesizer is run directly as the informed over-sampling method underlying the framework's class-imbalance handling.

paper-wearable-hydration-timegan-2023.summary: Generates synthetic wearable biosignals for hydration monitoring, where collecting labelled data means running controlled dehydration studies on human subjects, and evaluates whether a time-series GAN can stand in for that collection. The authors adopt TimeGAN, which is specific to sequential data, rather than a tabular generator, and assess the output on distributional similarity and downstream classification. CTGAN enters only as prior art: Xu et al. is cited for the general problem that tabular data mixes discrete and continuous columns, that such mixtures require applying both softmax and tanh at the generator output, and that modelling them realistically is non-trivial. Nothing from SDV is run, so the entry records CTGAN as the tabular line of work the paper departs from in choosing a time-series architecture.

paper-dbnex-deep-belief-network-2022.summary: This paper proposes DBNex, a fraud-detection pipeline that combines nonlinear dimensionality reduction (UMAP), DBSCAN clustering, and a Deep Belief Network classifier, aiming to address severe class imbalance in credit card fraud datasets. To mitigate the imbalance, the authors generate 500 synthetic fraud transactions and merge them with the original minority class before clustering and classification. CTGAN (the Conditional Tabular GAN) is run directly as the synthetic data generator producing the pseudo-fraud samples that underpin the class-balancing step of the whole pipeline.

paper-membership-inference-countermeasur.summary: This conference paper studies how blending a fully synthetic dataset with the original training data (a 'partially synthetic' approach) affects resistance to membership inference attacks versus model prediction accuracy, using post-randomization perturbation to generate the synthetic data. The authors find that partially perturbed datasets can achieve attack resistance comparable to fully perturbed ones while better preserving prediction accuracy. The paper cites the original SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) paper as related work on synthetic data generation, without indicating that the SDV software itself was used to produce the experimental data.

paper-sos-oversampling-2022.summary: Brings score-based generative models to tabular oversampling, redesigning the score network for table records and adding a style-transfer option that oversamples around the class boundary. CTGAN is among the ten baselines it is measured against across six datasets.

paper-tapas-toolbox-adversarial-privacy-.summary: This paper introduces TAPAS, an open-source toolbox implementing a general threat-modeling framework and a library of adversarial attacks for empirically evaluating the privacy of synthetic data generators. The authors apply TAPAS across several attack scenarios, testing it against three synthetic data generators with differing privacy guarantees. CTGAN is used as one of three generators (alongside PrivBayes and MST) whose synthetic outputs are subjected to the toolbox's privacy attacks.

paper-iot-intrusion-hadoop-spark-2022.summary: Builds an intrusion detection model over IoT network traffic on a distributed Hadoop and Spark stack, where detection quality is bounded by how few samples the rarer attack classes contribute. CTGAN generates the minority-class records in the BoT-IoT dataset, so SDV supplies the rebalancing step of a production-shaped security pipeline.

paper-wasserstein-generative-adversarial.summary: This paper proposes a double Wasserstein GAN approach for modeling marked temporal point processes, generating event types (categorical marks) conditioned on their times, and compares it against intensity-based point process models on synthetic and real-world datasets. In its related-work discussion, it describes CTGAN's conditional GAN approach to modeling tabular data with continuous and discrete values, noting its conditional vector encoding and its technique for handling data imbalance, without running the CTGAN code. SDV's CTGAN is only discussed conceptually as related prior art, not executed as part of the experiments.

The synthetic data generation approach targets incipient broken rotor bar detection where fault-free and faulty samples are scarce and unbalanced. CTGAN's original paper is cited only in the reference list as prior work on conditional GANs for tabular data, with no evidence it was run in the study.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-im.summary: The paper proposes GANSYN, a GAN-based oversampling method for predicting aging-related bugs (ARBs) in long-running software systems, addressing severe class imbalance across seven public ARB datasets and showing improved prediction performance over SMOTE, ADASYN, and other baselines. It targets scientific domains like weather and climate with complex, high-dimensional dependent structures rather than tabular data. paper-improving-privacy-synthetic-datase.summary: This paper proposes an instance-level Privacy Score based on a per-sample memorisation coefficient to help data sharers and auditors assess synthetic data privacy, showing empirically that membership-inference attack accuracy drops after filtering by this score on two real-world datasets. The authors generate synthetic versions of these datasets using five generative models -- CTGAN, WGAN-GP, PATEGAN, DPGAN, and RVAE -- describing each architecture's training dynamics and layer structure in detail. CTGAN (from the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN work) is one of several generators whose conditional-sampling training procedure is described and apparently reimplemented as part of this comparative generator suite, rather than invoked via the SDV library itself.

paper-dataset-designing-software-archite.summary: This conference paper proposes a novel dataset describing software architecture styles (e.g., Object Oriented, Client-Server, CORBA, Repository) so that researchers can apply data mining clustering algorithms to analyze software projects, and it demonstrates clustering with RapidMiner Studio on the proposed dataset. The SDV paper is cited only once in passing, as reference [1], to support the generic opening claim that 'Data is an important part of any software system,' with no further engagement anywhere in the text.

preprint-causal-augmentation-robust-fine.summary: This NeurIPS 2025 workshop paper proposes CausalMixFT, a method that fits Structural Causal Models on scarce target-dataset samples to generate structurally consistent synthetic examples for fine-tuning tabular foundation models, improving validation-based early stopping and downstream performance across 33 TabArena classification datasets. The authors compare their causal generator against several purely statistical synthetic-data augmentation baselines. CTGAN is run as one of several baseline generators (fit via a hyperparameter search including embedding_dim and related constructor parameters), and its mode-specific normalization approach is used to produce comparison synthetic data that CausalMixFT is shown to outperform.

preprint-disco-tab-hierarchical-reinforc.summary: This paper proposes DISCO-TAB, a framework that combines a fine-tuned LLM with a multi-objective, RL-trained discriminator system operating at token, sentence, feature, and row granularities to synthesize privacy-preserving clinical tabular data while resolving minority-class collapse. It is validated on medical and non-medical benchmarks (Heart Failure, Parkinson's, Obesity, etc.), reporting large gains in downstream classifier utility, statistical fidelity, and resistance to membership inference attacks over GAN, diffusion, and LLM-based baselines. CTGAN is run as one of several adversarial baselines throughout the empirical comparison tables, with the paper describing its conditional-vector approach to heterogeneous columns and citing it as a 'canonical baseline' that suffers from mode collapse on discrete, imbalanced clinical data.

paper-am-surface-roughness-cgan-2026.summary: Builds a predictor for arithmetic mean roughness in material-extrusion additive manufacturing from process parameters and local surface angle, trained on an 87-run Box-Behnken design, and wraps it in a web tool that renders predicted roughness over an uploaded 3D model so the effect of the staircase effect can be seen before printing. Conditional synthetic augmentation is added with a CGAN the authors build themselves; CTGAN is cited as the tabular conditional-GAN methodology their conditional generation follows, but it is not named in prose and not run.

preprint-sequential-tgan-generating-rela.summary: This preprint introduces Sequential RC-TGAN, a temporal extension of the RC-TGAN relational generator that adds a differentiable Spectral Envelope Theory loss to preserve periodic/seasonal structure in categorical and (via VGM discretization) continuous time series embedded in relational databases, and proposes two new spectral-divergence evaluation metrics. It is evaluated against several relational and time-series baselines including ClavaDDPM, DoppelGANger, and TimeGAN. SDV (its hierarchical Gaussian-copula relational model) is run as one of the comparison baselines in the experiments, where it is reported to consistently underperform at capturing temporal dynamics.

preprint-synthetic-homes-multimodal-gene.summary: This preprint presents a modular multimodal generative AI framework that combines publicly available records, imagery, and physics-based simulation to construct simulation-ready residential building energy datasets under data scarcity, validating plausibility against the ResStock national reference dataset. The SDV paper (Patki et al. 2016) is cited only as prior work on synthetic data evaluation philosophy when framing the authors' own plausibility-validation approach, with no SDV code run.

preprint-synthetic-network-packet-genera.summary: This paper proposes two constraint-enforcing synthetic data generation methods for IoT network intrusion detection: a statistical method combining PCA-based latent sampling with One-Class SVM/Isolation Forest boundary enforcement, and a genetic-algorithm method treating packet generation as multi-objective optimization, both evaluated on the ACI IoT 2023 dataset for class-imbalance amplification. CTGAN is discussed in related work as a conditional GAN variant for class-specific tabular synthesis and referenced via a prior study evaluating it alongside TabDDPM and GReaT, but no SDV-family code is run in the proposed pipeline. CTGAN is cited only as prior art the authors' own constraint-based methods are positioned against.

preprint-enabled-rent-seeking-how-2025.summary: This paper develops a dynamic economic model of how generative AI reshapes rent-seeking behavior and social welfare, analyzing effects like increased transparency alongside new manipulation and algorithmic interference risks, and proposes policy interventions such as taxation and regulation. The authors run theoretical analysis and multi-agent simulations to explore equilibrium outcomes under different regulatory policies. CTGAN is cited only as an example of prior work on market simulation applications, not used in the paper's own methodology.

preprint-embedding-driven-diversity-samp.summary: This preprint proposes an embedding-driven diversity-sampling method that selects a small set of real clinical notes to guide few-shot prompting of large language models, producing synthetic clinical text with greater syntactic diversity than random few-shot or zero-shot prompting. Evaluated on the CheXpert dataset, the approach improves downstream classification AUROC/AUPRC and reduces the real data needed to reach target performance. CTGAN is cited only in passing, in a background sentence noting that prior work used GANs and variational autoencoders to generate synthetic clinical data.

preprint-evaluating-privacy-utility-trad.summary: This preprint benchmarks four synthetic data generation methods—WGAN, CTGAN, a diffusion model, and Gaussian noise augmentation—for producing privacy-preserving smart-meter data used to classify households' suitability for dynamic Time-of-Use electricity tariffs, evaluating classification utility, distribution fidelity, and resistance to reconstruction and membership-inference attacks. CTGAN is run directly via SDV's CTGANSynthesizer with a SingleTableMetadata schema as one of the four generators compared, and its full-synthetic variant is found to offer the strongest privacy protection despite slightly lower utility than diffusion models.

preprint-sagda-open-source-synthetic-202.summary: This paper presents SAGDA, an open-source Python library for generating, augmenting, and validating synthetic agricultural datasets for African contexts, describing modules for data generation, modeling, augmentation, validation, and simulation, with use cases in yield prediction and NPK fertilizer recommendation. CTGAN and TGAN are cited only in a background sentence noting that synthetic data generation methods can help augment limited datasets without compromising privacy, with no evidence they are used within SAGDA's own implementation.

preprint-throwing-vines-wall-structure-2.summary: This paper proposes random search algorithms and a model-confidence-set framework for vine copula structure learning, challenging the long-standing dominance of Dissmann's greedy heuristic and demonstrating consistent empirical gains on real-world datasets for generative modeling and regression tasks. It surveys prior applications of vine copulas across many domains, listing the SDV-family vine copula synthetic-data paper (Sun, Cuesta-Infante, and Veeramachaneni, 2019) among several cited works on generative modeling, without running or extending it.

preprint-contextual-chart-generation-cyb.summary: This paper introduces HoneyPlotNet, a multi-modal generative system combining a multitask Transformer and a specialized autoencoder to automatically produce realistic charts (captions, plot text, and underlying tabular data) for honeyfiles used in cyber deception. It also releases a new document-chart dataset and a Keyword Semantic Matching metric to evaluate semantic consistency. CTGAN is cited only in a related-work discussion grouping several tabular data generation models as prior art whose design assumes uniform data structure and simplistic categorical treatment, without being run or extended.

preprint-dall-context-aware-clinical-202.summary: DALL-M is a framework that augments clinical tabular datasets by combining structured patient data (vitals, radiology findings, demographics) with contextual knowledge from radiology reports and domain resources using LLMs, expanding 9 clinical features to 91 on MIMIC-IV cases and improving downstream ML model performance. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no evidence it was run or engaged with in the text.

paper-macode-masked-density-2024.summary: Recasts masked language modelling over discretised tabular columns as histogram-based non-parametric conditional density estimation, showing that minimising the multi-class classification loss corresponds to minimising a divergence between the true and modelled conditional densities, which yields MaCoDE as a single model that generates across arbitrary combinations of target and conditional variables, supports multiple imputation under several missingness mechanisms, and tunes privacy by a sampling temperature without retraining. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the seven compared generators, run from the sdv-dev repository at default hyperparameters with the latent dimension aligned to 100 for a fair size comparison.

paper-tabcutmix-memorization-2024.summary: Gives the first systematic study of memorization in tabular diffusion models, showing that near-identical training rows are replicated more as training lengthens and as the dataset shrinks, and proposes TabCutMix and TabCutMixPlus, which swap feature subsets between same-class training rows, the Plus variant restricting swaps to correlation-clustered features, to cut replication without losing sample quality. The evaluation is run on SDMetrics: the shape and trend scores are its KSComplement and TVComplement metrics and the machine learning efficacy metrics are taken from the same package, while CTGAN and TVAE are two of the generators the mitigation is shown to carry over to.

paper-unmasking-trees-2024.summary: Presents UnmaskingTrees, which fits gradient-boosted decision trees to incrementally unmask individual features for tabular imputation and generation, together with BaltoBot, a balanced-tree conditional density estimator that turns any probabilistic binary classifier into a generative model, and reports leading imputation performance on a 27-dataset out-of-the-box benchmark. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the compared generators: the paper repeats the experimental setup of Jolicoeur-Martineau et al. and reports their average ranks across nine metrics both on complete data and under 20 percent missingness.

preprint-varppud-variant-post-prioritiza.summary: This preprint introduces VarPPUD, a machine-learning tool trained on gene-, amino acid-, and nucleotide-level features to distinguish disease-causing variants from other deleterious candidates prioritized in Undiagnosed Diseases Network (UDN) cases, improving on traditional pathogenicity predictors. To further validate the model, the authors used CTGAN to generate additional synthetic variants from unimputed UDN feature vectors, applying constraint design to keep synthesized values within valid ranges and types. CTGAN is run as an auxiliary data-generation step to test VarPPUD's discriminative ability on synthetic, GAN-generated candidate variants.

paper-realtabformer-relational-2023.summary: Generates relational datasets with transformers rather than statistical models: a GPT-style model learns the parent table, and a sequence-to-sequence model conditioned on the frozen parent encoding produces the child rows, with an overfitting criterion based on a statistical bootstrap deciding when to stop training. SDV is the relational baseline the result is measured against — the paper identifies the Hierarchical Modeling Algorithm of Patki et al., which fits Gaussian copulas within and across tables, as the existing approach for relational synthesis, and its figures plot SDV's output beside REaLTabFormer's on the parent-child joint distributions and on a daily sales series.

paper-data-iq-subgroups-2022.summary: Separates a training set into easy, ambiguous and hard examples by tracking each example's predictive confidence and aleatoric uncertainty across training epochs, so that irreducible label noise can be told apart from model-side uncertainty and subgroups with heterogeneous outcomes surfaced. One experiment applies this to choosing between synthetic datasets: CTGAN and Gaussian Copula stand in for two synthetic data vendors, both run from the sdv-dev implementation, and the paper reports that the generator producing the higher proportion of easy examples is the one whose data trains the better real-data classifier.

paper-dtgan-dp-tabular-2021.summary: Asks where differential privacy should be enforced in a tabular GAN, and answers it by building two variants of DTGAN that apply DP-SGD with subsampled Renyi accounting to the discriminator and to the generator respectively, showing that noising the discriminator gives the better utility-privacy trade-off and that DP-SGD outperforms the PATE framework on three datasets against PATE-GAN and DP-WGAN. CTGAN's conditional architecture is what the generator-side privacy argument rests on: the generator loss is described as a by-product of that architecture, which makes the conditional vector independent of the real training data, but CTGAN itself is neither run nor compared against.

preprint-airline-passenger-name-record-2.summary: This work proposes a GAN-based method (Cramér GAN with categorical feature embedding and a Cross-Net architecture) to generate realistic synthetic Passenger Name Records for airlines, addressing data-sharing and privacy constraints in the travel industry, and evaluates it on a real PNR dataset for distribution matching, memorization, and downstream predictive tasks. For encoding numerical features, the authors adopt the Gaussian-sampling discretization technique proposed by Patki et al. (2016), the Synthetic Data Vault paper, implementing it in their own pipeline rather than running SDV's software.

repo-generative-trace-tutorials.summary: Tutorial material from the CMU NetShare group for AINTEC 2025, teaching generative models over network trace datasets on prepared server environments. SDV is installed from source rather than PyPI: `src/ctgan` and `src/sdmetrics` are checked in and installed editable from `requirements.txt`, tab-ddpm brings a second CTGAN copy under `src/tabddpm/CTGAN`, and the notebooks `network_ctgan.ipynb` and `tabular_CTGAN.ipynb` fit `CTGAN` on trace and tabular data. CTGAN's and SDMetrics' sources are vendored and run as the tutorial's worked baseline.
